title: SSE/WSS multiplex + churn load driver for realistic streaming chat benchmarks
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a production-grade load driver that simulates realistic streaming chat traffic over Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket (WSS) transports at large scale. The driver should model tokens/sec emission, session churn, reconnection/backoff behavior, KV-cache warmup, prefix caching, and multiplexing (multiple logical user sessions per TCP connection). Outputs feed into automated regression detection that flags deviations in p95 latency, tokens/sec, and stream completeness versus a baseline run.
background: Existing streaming load tooling focuses on simple fanout or synthetic constant-rate streams. Production traffic has: variable tokens/sec per session, mid-stream reconnections, partial message fragmentation, prefix cache warmup behavior that affects p95, and high correlation between connection churn and backend tail latency. We need a harness that reproduces these properties so performance regressions affecting streaming chat are detected before rollouts.
goals: Simulate 100k concurrent logical sessions across a configurable fleet of driver agents using SSE and WSS
Model tokens/sec distributions (long-tail) and produce per-session token emission traces replayable from production telemetry
Include realistic session churn (connect/disconnect/reconnect), exponential backoff, and transient network errors
Support multiplexing mode: N logical sessions per TCP connection to exercise connection pooling and proxy behavior
Produce metrics required for regression detection: tokens/sec, p95 token latency, p99, stream-complete rate, error rate, connection success rate
Integrate with Redwood Console dashboards and CI to run baseline and candidate comparisons with auto-alerting
acceptance_criteria: Driver can run a 30-minute baseline scenario that produces reproducible metrics within ±3% tokens/sec on repeat runs
Regression detection pipeline computes deltas vs baseline and raises an alert when p95 increases by >10% or tokens/sec drops by >5% for two consecutive runs
Harness supports both SSE and WSS transports with identical scenario definitions
Multiplexing is configurable (1..50 logical sessions per connection) and shows measurable effect on connection count vs per-session CPU/latency
Artifacts (dashboard, PRs, baseline data) exist and are linked in the ticket
technical_approach: Driver architecture will follow a controller/agent model. Controller orchestrates scenarios, distributes session traces and profiles to agents, and aggregates telemetry. Agents are lightweight Go binaries that open SSE or WebSocket connections, replay token emission traces (with configurable jitter), and optionally multiplex multiple logical sessions on a single physical connection. Agents emit Prometheus metrics and structured events (JSON) to a Kafka topic used by the regression detector. Regression detector applies statistical tests (moving-window percent change + CUSUM for persistent shifts) and publishes findings to the Console and Slack. Baseline runs are versioned and stored in S3 with metadata (model, sequence length distribution, kv-cache warmed boolean).
implementation_tasks: T1 - Controller scaffolding: scenario API, job scheduling, and agent health (ENG-33021.1)
T2 - Agent SSE client: reconnect/backoff, chunked message assembly, prefix cache warmup hooks (ENG-33021.2)
T3 - Agent WSS client: per-message fragmentation, TLS session reuse, multiplexing mode (ENG-33021.3)
T4 - Trace loader: ingest production session traces (anonymized) and synthesize variable token rhythms for replay (ENG-33021.4)
T5 - Metrics pipeline: Prometheus + Kafka exporter + regression detector consumer (ENG-33021.5)
T6 - Dashboard: pre-built Grafana/Console dashboard with tokens/sec, p95/p99, connection churn, and stream-complete heatmap (ENG-33021.6)
T7 - CI integration: nightly baseline run and candidate comparison job with automatic Slack alerts and PR comment integration (ENG-33021.7)
T8 - Chaos scenarios: intermittent proxy 5xx injection and graceful reconnect verification (ENG-33021.8)
T9 - Load optimization: agent batching of messages and TCP connection pooling heuristics (ENG-33021.9)
T10 - Docs + Runbook: how to run a baseline, interpret regressions, and triage (ENG-33021.10)
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Serving and Console teams. Decided on controller/agent split and Prometheus+Kafka telemetry stack. Marcus to prototype agent SSE client.

2026-02-28: Prototype agent implemented in Go that opens 2000 SSE connections on a single m5.4xlarge; observed connection limit issues from AWS ENI, added per-agent connection cap and multiplexing plan.
2026-03-03: Trace loader MVP imports anonymized production traces (seq length + token timings) and can synthesize jittered replay. Initial baseline run produced tokens/sec within ±4% across 3 runs.
2026-03-08: Regression detector skeleton using percent-change + CUSUM implemented; first smoke alerts generated for an intentional 15% p95 increase in canary run.
2026-03-10: Added multiplexing mode to agent (N=8 tested). Observed 22% reduction in ephemeral connection count and a small p95 improvement; need to validate across model variants and proxy setups.
review_feedback: PM (Leah Ortiz): Ensure baseline metadata includes model hash, kv-cache state, and upstream proxy config. Add customer-impact tagging for runs used in SLA-related investigations.
Security (Samir Kaur): Agents must support mTLS to connect to controller and rotate agent credentials via KMS. Add security_review_required flag on PRs.
SRE (Diego Morales): Add control for peak connection ramp rate to avoid inducing infra-wide failure during large-scale runs. Include a kill-switch in controller.
risks: Driver can itself become an operational blast radius if ramped too quickly; need kill-switch and rate-limits
Agent connection quotas on cloud instances (ENI / ephemeral ports) limit single-agent scale; multiplexing mitigates but must be well-tested
False positives from natural production variance — regression detector thresholds must be tuned with multiple baselines
next_steps: Stabilize multiplexing heuristics across AWS, GCP, and on-prem proxy variants
Wire mTLS and KMS agent credential rotation per security feedback
Run an end-to-end baseline across three model families (small, medium, llama-variant) and publish baselines to S3
Add load-shedding experiment to verify graceful degradation and fallback policies when KV cache coldness causes p95 spikes
notes: Use production traces only after anonymization pipeline (PM-248) completes
Consider adding a lightweight WASM-based agent for low-footprint edge workers
Coordinate run windows with Capacity and Sales for Dedicated customers to avoid SLA impact
